title: Quorum: speed vs accuracy in collective decision-making

hypothesis.statement: Requiring a larger quorum before deciding trades speed for accuracy with diminishing returns; when the agents' evaluations share a bias (correlated error), increasing the quorum does not correct the error and accuracy saturates below the independent case.

predictions.text: In every cell, accuracy is non-decreasing in Q (tolerance 1 p.p.) and mean time to decision is strictly increasing in Q.
Diminishing returns: in the cells where the accuracy gain from Q=1 to Q=50 is > 5 p.p., at least 50% of that gain is already obtained with Q <= 10.
With shared bias (rho=0.5), accuracy at Q=50 is lower than with rho=0 (same sigma, Delta; disjoint 95% CIs) and the gain from Q=20 to Q=50 is < 2 p.p. (plateau).
Harder discrimination (Delta=0.1) has lower accuracy than Delta=0.25 at every Q, for each (sigma, rho).

quality-weighted-recruitment.status: v1.1.0 post-hoc amendment; main regime of the tests

params.perception: q_hat = q_j + sigma*(sqrt(rho)*B_j + sqrt(1-rho)*e_i), B_j ~ N(0,1) per site and per run (shared bias)
params.quorum_note: decision = first site whose number of committed agents reaches Q; the dynamics do not change with Q (observed quorum), so all Q values use the same run
